extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedians / Wikipedia editors contributing to mathematics articles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating, improving, classifying, and maintaining mathematics articles on English Wikipedia. Covers article scope, style/conventions, assessment categories, and common editorial tasks (stubs, references, links, pseudo-mathematics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 'bare bones' format for mathematical articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a standard 'bare bones' format for mathematical articles to assist creation, improvement and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project originally aimed to provide a standard bare-bones format; use the house style for mathematical articles and the indices/lists maintained by the project to organize content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add at least an approximate mathematical category
rubrics_metrics.description: When contributing new articles which are (even only remotely) related to mathematics, please add at least an approximate mathematical category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding a category enables identification, review, and further editing by the project (it lists the article in indices and increases the chance editors will expand it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring stubs up to a reasonable standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Many pages are definition-only; editors should bring stubs up to a reasonable standard rather than leaving bare definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add motivation and examples, expand beyond a bare definition, and improve structure so the article is more than a single definitional sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop articles into good expositions (add motivation, history, attributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Important articles should be developed into good expositions, not just statements of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bridge the gap between stating facts and teaching: add motivation, illustrative examples, history, and proper attributions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand coverage and update advanced material
rubrics_metrics.description: Work to expand coverage to bring subjects up-to-date, especially advanced material that needs expert contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a large task that requires patience and determination; experts are encouraged to contribute to modernize and expand advanced topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep track of articles by listing, categorising, and assessing them
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain lists and categories of mathematics articles and assess their importance and quality to track progress and identify weak spots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the project's indices, lists by topic, and the maths rating template on article talk pages to record assessments and suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use maths rating templates to assess quality and suggest improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are assessed by placing (or updating) a maths rating template on the talk page of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template provides an opportunity to add a brief comment suggesting improvements; anyone can rate an article (except GA/FA which require nomination processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality grade categories (FA, FL, FM, GA, B, C, Start, Stub, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics articles are classified by quality using a set of grades: FA, FL, FM, GA, B, C, Start, Stub, List, Draft, Category, Disambig, File, Portal, Project, Redirect, Template, NA, Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grades summarize the state-of-play and are used to identify which articles can be improved or nominated for Good Article / Featured Article status. FA and GA should only be added after standard nomination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance rating categories (Top/High/Mid/Low/NA/???)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are also classified by importance: Top, High, Mid, Low, NA, ??? (unknown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importance classifications help prioritize work and identify coverage gaps across the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and report pseudo-mathematics, hoaxes, and unattributable material
rubrics_metrics.description: Project members should identify crankery, hoaxes, and material with dubious or unverifiable sources and report them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anything suspect should be reported on the talk page of the article so editors can discuss and remove or correct it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address reader-level difficulty: start simple then move to abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing for a general readership, start simple and then move toward more abstract and general statements as the article proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider what background the reader may have; introduce basic concepts first, then generalize. This approach helps accessibility and pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: When describing a concept via another, add a prominent link and a quick naive explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you describe a concept in terms of another (e.g., rational numbers in terms of integers), add a prominent link to the relevant article and, if it makes sense, a very quick (naive) explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid duplicate links. If the related article doesn't exist, create a good stub (see stub guidance). The goal is to make cross-references useful to readers at different levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a related article is missing, create a good stub and add a category
rubrics_metrics.description: When a relevant article does not exist, create a good stub and add a mathematical category so it appears in lists and indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating a stub increases visibility (e.g., in the list of mathematics articles) and increases the chance that other editors will expand it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check existing articles for established terminology and propose changes on talk pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminology can vary; check pre-existing related articles to see if there is established usage before changing terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you propose changes in terminology or usage, raise them on the article's talk page or this project's talk page for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Manual of Style for mathematics and related conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Wikipedia:Manual of Style (mathematics) and related pages (Mathematical conventions, Naming conventions for theorems, Algorithms on Wikipedia, Scientific citation guidelines) for style and notation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pages describe conventions for mathematical notation, naming, formatting formulas (wikified HTML and TeX), and citation practices — consult them when writing or editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use problem tag templates and bot/manual cleanup listings to flag and fix issues (references, cleanup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag articles needing attention with problem tag templates and address issues listed by bot/manual cleanup listings (e.g., reference problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Wikipedia:Template index/Cleanup for tags to apply. There are bot-generated cleanup lists and PetScan queries to find pages needing attention; use them to coordinate fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: focus on articles primarily mathematical while acknowledging overlaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics includes overlaps with physics, computer science, operations research, and other areas, but the project's focus is on articles which are primarily mathematical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a topic is primarily in another field and covered by a separate WikiProject, consider coordinating with that project; where overlap exists, ensure the mathematical viewpoint is clear and appropriately scoped.
